subject: Planned rolling kernel & IO maintenance — North US targeted window and fallback operations
messages:
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0400
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmecloud.com>, ops-team@acmecloud.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Subject: Planned rolling kernel & IO maintenance — North US targeted window and fallback operations

Hi Tom / Acme ops team,

We wanted to give you early notice of a planned, low-risk maintenance window in our North US cluster that will include a rolling kernel and IO driver update plus targeted host evacuations. The goal is to address a compatibility regression we observed at scale for certain NIC firmware versions and to proactively refresh IO paths before the heavier holiday traffic.

High-level window
- When: Oct 14 23:00 — Oct 15 06:00 EDT (rolling over multiple availability zones to avoid a single-region outage)
- Expected impact: brief (~30–90s) connection handoffs for affected GPUs during host swap; transient request retries expected. No data plane migration is required for pinned private deployments.

Key safeguards and fallback plan
- We will perform sequential host evacuations with KV-cache warmups on failover targets to preserve inference latency for live sessions where possible.
- If a node exhibits unexpected IO path failures, requests will be routed to a compatible model variant in a separate host pool (automatic fallback).
- Our rollback window is 30 minutes per host; if rollback is required we will restore the previous kernel image and re-route traffic.

Action items for AcmeCloud
1) Please confirm whether you require an opt-out for any customer projects pinned to the zone(s) listed in the runbook.
2) Provide a primary on-call contact for Oct 14 overnight (name + cell).

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v2.docx (runbook), kv-cache-preservation-matrix.pdf

I'll follow up with the canary schedule and the list of AZs we'll touch. If you'd prefer a short sync before the window, I can set up a 20m call.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

2) Fallback model variant: what's the TTF (time to failover) you expect for active requests; will it be automatic or require a client retry?

Also, our on-call for that night will be me (Tom) — cell +1-415-555-0123.

If you can share the canary list and expected AZ order, we can validate our affinity rules.

Best,

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0400
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmecloud.com>, ops-team@acmecloud.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Planned rolling kernel & IO maintenance — North US targeted window and fallback operations

Tom — great, thanks for confirming your on-call. Answers below and a short checklist: 

1) KV cache persistence
- Sessions labeled "chat:sticky" and "session:longrun" in your tenant mapping will receive KV rehydration attempts. We add a 2-step warmup: (a) pre-copy of popular prefixes to the failover host, (b) on-first-request shallow fetch to reduce tail latency. We cannot guarantee full KV parity for very large working set sessions; where customers require exact continuity we recommend a temporary pin to a non-evacuated host (opt-out). See kv-cache-preservation-matrix.pdf (page 2) for mapping.

2) Fallback behavior and timing
- TTF: typical automatic routing to fallback pool is 8–20s for in-flight token streams; for streaming sessions we will attempt to resume but clients may need to reconnect.
- Fallback is automatic at the edge level; clients that implement retry-on-5xx with an exponential backoff will see a faster recovery.

Canary schedule and AZ order
- Canary 1: Oct 14 23:00 — az-north-1a (small set of hosts)
- Canary 2: Oct 14 23:30 — az-north-1b
- Ramp: Oct 15 00:15 — az-north-1c then staggered across remaining hosts through 06:00

Customer opt-outs
- If you need to opt any workload out, please reply with tenant IDs by Oct 13 18:00 EDT.

Runbook links: https://redwood.app/notes/PR-1456-maintenance-runbook (runbook), https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-10-12-northus-maintenance

Let me know if you'd like a 20m prep call today at 11:00. I'll also copy Ben — he'll lead the rollback/drivers if we trigger that path.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah / team — quick internal confirmation thread before I send the final customer note and canary invite: 

1) Canary payload: run a mix that exercises large-KV warmups (labels: chat:sticky, session:longrun) + short-latency smoke tests. Ben will verify the KV pre-copy script runs against the canary pool at 22:30.
2) Monitoring hooks: Grace, can you ensure the trace alert thresholds are set to 25% above baseline for tail-p99 latency and set an automatic rollback ticket if p99 > 1.8s for >10 minutes?
3) Support play: I will publish the short-run SLA advisory on the status page and include Tom's contact. Hannah, please confirm opt-out deadline and include the file names (maintenance_runbook_v2.docx, kv-cache-preservation-matrix.pdf).

If no objections, I'll send the finalized customer update at 17:00 and push a public status update.

Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
